task_text: Push Slider: A wall stands in front of the hovering aerial manipulator, with a horizontal slider mounted on its front face: a straight rail about 1 m long and a red knob that slides along it. The knob starts at the rail's left end (as seen from the robot facing the wall) and must be pushed along the rail until it is within 5 cm of the right end of its travel, i.e. at least 0.95 m along its 1 m travel. Success: Success when the slider's prismatic joint SliderJoint has position >= 0.45 m (slider_pushed_threshold; the joint ranges from -0.5 m to 0.5 m and starts at -0.5 m), i.e. the knob has travelled at least 0.95 m from its start toward world -y (the robot's right). AM-Bench also reports a subtask criterion slider_engaged (joint position - start >= 0.05 x (0.45 - (-0.5)) = 0.0475 m); it is informational only. Evaluated after every control step (decimation 1, so after every 1/120 s physics step) on the simulated state; no hold time is required. The episode terminates at the first step where it holds. Otherwise it is truncated by the time limit: episode_length_s = 26 s, i.e. max_episode_length = 3120 control steps; AM-Bench raises the time-out when episode_length_buf >= max_episode_length - 1, i.e. at the 3119th step.
episode: one episode, no reset: it ends at the first control step where AM-Bench's success check holds, when the task's episode length of 26 s of simulated time runs out (AM-Bench's time-out, at control step 3119), when your time is up, or on a simulator error; the simulated clock advances only with the control steps you run
